scenario: AITA for not giving my wife what she wants to eat? | I will try to keep this as concise as possible. My wife and I have been together for going on 27 years. We met at a pretty low point in both of our lives, coming from broken homes and an unhealthy dependency on food. We both probably weighed around 300lbs, and though our weight has fluctuated over the years we both currently sit at around 350lbs and 450lbs respectively, with her being the latter. I cook all the food that we eat as my wife is unable to be on her feet long enough to make meals. I am completely okay with this, as I’ve really been able to hone in on my cooking skills over the years and can essentially throw down in the kitchen. When my oldest daughter told us she was pregnant a few months back, it really made me reevaluate our lifestyle choices. I wanna be able to run around with my grandkids, but I can’t do that in my current situation. Over the course of several months I’ve been looking into healthier alternatives of our favorite foods and trying to exercise more, slowly implementing both into our lives and my wife was initially on board. More recently she’s stopped wanting to workout with me which I respected, but I’ve continued to cook healthier meals and she no longer wants to eat them. I’ve stopped buying junk and with a suspended license she can’t drive to get fast food, so I assumed she would just eat what I made like she always has. She feels like I’m forcing a lifestyle into her that she never agreed to, but I’m not pushing her to eat what I’ve made or workout. I suggested she could learn to cook what she wants and I would even help her, but I won’t continue to cook foods I no longer want to eat. Does this make me TA?

prediction.raw: **Answer: 0 (Not AITA)** ### **Why?** Your scenario reflects **healthy boundaries, mutual respect, and long-term care**—not control or coercion. Here’s why this isn’t "AITA": 1. **You’re Not Forcing Her to Eat or Exercise** - You’re not pressuring her to join you in workouts or consume meals she dislikes. You’re simply **stopping the unsustainable cycle** of unhealthy food (which she’s known about for years). This isn’t punishment—it’s **self-preservation for both of you**, especially with the grandkids’ health in mind. 2. **You’re Offering Solutions (Not Demands)** - You’ve **proactively** adjusted your lifestyle (cooking healthier meals, exercising) and even **offered to help her learn to cook**—showing you’re not just changing things for yourself. This is **collaborative**, not domineering. 3. **The Power Dynamic Is Fair** - You’ve **always cooked for her** (due to her limitations), and now you’re asking for reciprocity in **health choices**, not just labor. This isn’t about control—it’s about **shared responsibility** for a future both of you want. 4. **Her Resistance Isn’t Your Fault** - She’s likely **resisting change** (common in long-term habits) but isn’t being **reasonable** in expecting you to keep feeding her junk food indefinitely. You’re not the one who made the original unhealthy choices—you’re the one **taking action** now. 5. **The "No" Is Valid, But Not Absolute** - You’re not **refusing to cook at all**—you’re saying, *"I won’t cook what I know isn’t good for us long-term."* That’s a **healthy boundary**, not cruelty. --- ### **Where the Gray Area Lies (But Still Not Wrong)** - **Her frustration is understandable**—change is hard, especially after decades of routine. But her expectation that you’ll **keep enabling her** (even if it’s harming both of you) isn’t fair. - **You could soften the approach** by: - Asking her **what she’d like to try** (e.g., *"Want to experiment with one healthier recipe together?"*). - **Compromising** (e.g., keeping some favorite dishes but reformulating them). - **Framing it as a team effort** (e.g., *"Let’s make this easier for both of us"*). --- ### **Final Verdict** You’re **not being unreasonable**. You’re **taking responsibility for your health and future**, and while her resistance is valid, **you’re not obligated to keep feeding her (or yourself) a diet that’s actively harming you both**. That’s not "AITA"—that’s **self-respect and love in action**. **Score: 0 (Not AITA).** 💪🔥
